title: How we know it is right
lead: Every number on this page is read from the committed validation file. Nothing here is typed by hand.
exampleBanner: This is the example file. The measured values are still empty, so the tables show the shape of the check, not its result.

verdict.heading: The short answer
verdict.world: Added across the world, our total lands within about {errors} per cent of the reference on the {tests} hold-out tests.
verdict.large: For the countries that burn most, a typical country is out by about {error} per cent.
verdict.small: For the countries that burn least, a typical country is out by about {error} per cent, which is too much to rely on.

verdict.counted: {scored} countries were scored; {thin} had too little fire to judge.
verdict.readAs: Read a world or regional total as sound, a large country as usable, and a small country as a rough guide. The tables below show where each figure comes from.

dataText.v2: no S-NPP row of a test's prediction years is used while fitting or predicting that test
dataText.v3: Ratio of sums of the reference sensor over the older one per country, 5 degree latitude band and calendar month, pulled towards the country and then the world average, plus a background term for cell-months where the older sensor saw nothing.
dataText.v4: The independent test covered two countries and fitted on those two. The app's numbers come from the same model fitted on all 235 countries, whose own test is still being run.
dataText.v5: The model the app uses, fitted on every country and tested on years it had never seen. Percentiles run across the countries with enough fire to score; the groups are equal thirds of those countries by how much they burn. coverage_in_range is the share of countries whose stated range really held 80 to 97 per cent of the test values. The pooled row adds every country together month by month.
dataText.v10: Our measured worldwide S-NPP to MODIS fire-cell-day ratio.
dataText.v11: the scorer's hand-computed truth samples match the raw files
dataText.v13: exported tile totals equal the conversion's own totals
dataText.v14: checked by the contract test at export time
dataText.v17: Harmonized numbers exist per 0.25 degree cell, about 28 km across. A smaller area still reports the whole cell, so it is labelled low confidence.
dataText.v18: The model the app uses was fitted on all 235 countries and then tested on years it had never seen, for every country. Those results are the world scope on this page, and each country's own result is there too. Separately, the choice between two conversion methods was decided on Bulgaria and the United States, because that comparison needed hand-checked truth.
dataText.v19: The 2026 months are provisional. They come from near-real-time data and can still change as the full records are published.
dataText.v20: November 2026 holds 14 days, not a whole month, so it must not be compared with a full month. It carries the flag partial_month.
dataText.v21: A country total for the newest months is slightly low. Some detections have no country assigned yet, so they appear in the map cells but in no country file. It was about 1.5 per cent of the 2026 cell-days.
dataText.v22: A small country has a wide range. Across Bulgaria's estimated months the upper end sits about 3.8 times the value, while for the United States it is about 1.25 times. That is the model's honest spread once it is pooled across 235 countries: fewer fires mean less to learn from, so the range widens. Nothing has been narrowed to make it look better.
dataText.v23: A yearly or worldwide range is the sum of the monthly ranges underneath it. Adding ranges that way assumes every month is wrong in the same direction at once, which is unlikely, so a total's range is wider than the truth needs. Read a total's range as an outer bound, not as a likely spread.
dataText.v24: One world-gate check was missed: the Bulgaria error on the first hold-out at country level is above the limit we set ourselves. It is reported here rather than hidden, and the team decided to go ahead.
dataText.v25: A single 0.25 degree cell in a single month is far less reliable than a region or a country. The error at cell level is several times the error at country level, which is why the app shows a range.
dataText.v26: Nothing like VIIRS flew before 20 January 2012. Values before February 2012 are converted from MODIS and carry a range, not a single certain number.
dataText.v27: Before February 2012 a cell that lists no fire for a month still carries a small background value, because the old sensors often saw nothing where the newer one would have seen fire.
dataText.v28: Counts over fewer than eight days are strongly biased by the satellite's orbit, so the app never compares a run shorter than that.
dataText.v29: The daily numbers are raw counts from the sensor flying at the time, not converted ones, so a year before 2012 cannot be compared with a later year without scaling. The app marks those years estimated.
dataText.v30: Country files use the data provider's own country for each detection, so cells on a border can differ slightly from a drawn outline.
dataText.v31: Static industrial heat sources are filtered out, so gas flares and similar sites are not counted as fires.
dataText.v32: Fire radiative power is the reference sensor's own total, not converted between sensors, so it steps at the sensor change.
dataText.v33: This is a research prototype built from past detections. It is not an official warning service.
